title: Dividing a Decimal by a Whole Number

steps.body: Estimate the quotient before dividing. Sharing 1.44 among 4 groups should give a little more than 0.3 in each group.
steps.narration: Estimate the quotient before dividing. Sharing 1.44 among 4 groups should give a little more than 0.3 in each group.

widget.lowFeedback: Too low — a quarter of about one and a half is more than a few hundredths.
widget.highFeedback: Too high — sharing 1.44 four ways cannot leave more than half a unit in each part.

predict.prompt: Sharing 1.44 into 4 parts, is each part more or less than 1?
predict.reveal: Four equal parts of one and a bit must each be well under a whole unit.

cml.actionGoal: Work in the smallest place the numbers use, then decide where the point belongs for g5dc div whole.
invariants: A decimal is place value continued past the ones: computing in the smallest shared place turns g5dc div whole into whole-number arithmetic, and the point's position records which place the digits landed in.
misconceptions: Right-aligning digits instead of the points, treating a trailing zero as a change in value, or losing count of the decimal places a product carries.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the point moved one place left, how many times smaller would the amount become?

commonErrors.feedback: 275 hundredths is the WHOLE amount; the question asks what one of 5 equal parts holds.
Subtracting removes one part's worth once; sharing equally is division.
